outputs: Adversarially perturbed machine-generated text that evades detection while preserving fluency and semantic consistency

changes_made.explanation: Removed tasks that are not actually evaluated as NLG tasks in this paper (the paper uses existing generated text from these domains but doesn't generate new summaries/answers/abstracts). Removed models that are used for detection/proxy scoring, not for text generation. Consolidated dataset variations.
Normalized case variations and removed duplicates. The paper uses these metrics to evaluate the effectiveness of the adversarial attacks on detection systems.
No LLMs were used as judges/evaluators in this paper. LLMs were used for generation and proxy tasks, but not for evaluation of outputs.

guideline: MTurk workers evaluated whether RAFT-perturbed text remained indistinguishable from human-written text in terms of fluency and semantic consistency

changes_made.explanation: The extracted metadata was accurate. Human evaluation was conducted via Amazon Mechanical Turk to assess text quality preservation.

overall_notes: This paper focuses on adversarial attacks against LLM detection systems, not on generating NLG outputs for traditional tasks. The NLG aspect comes from perturbing existing machine-generated text to evade detection. The paper uses pre-generated text from various domains (summarization, QA, abstracts) but doesn't actually perform those NLG tasks - it modifies existing generated text. The automatic metrics evaluate detection evasion effectiveness rather than traditional NLG quality.
